# One-sample t-test power analysis
# H0: mu = 0 vs H1: mu > 0 (one-sided)
# Effect size (Cohen's d) = mean_diff / sd

library(stats)

mean_diff <- 0.2
sd_value <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
sidedness <- 1  # one-sided

# Cohen's d effect size
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd_value

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Effect size (mean difference):", mean_diff, "units\n")
cat("Standard deviation:", sd_value, "units\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("Alpha (significance level):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Test type: One-sided one-sample t-test\n\n")

# Function to calculate power for one-sample t-test
# Given: effect size d, sample size n, alpha, sidedness
power_one_sample_t <- function(n, d, alpha, sidedness) {
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n)
  
  # Degrees of freedom
  df <- n - 1
  
  # For one-sided test
  if (sidedness == 1) {
    # Upper-tail critical value
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
    # Power = P(t > t_crit | H1)
    power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)
  } else {
    # Two-sided test
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
    power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)
  }
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n that achieves target power
# Start with a reasonable estimate and search upward
n_range <- 1:200

powers <- sapply(n_range, function(n) power_one_sample_t(n, cohens_d, alpha, sidedness))

# Find minimum n with power >= target_power
min_n <- min(n_range[powers >= target_power])

# Get power at the minimum n and at n-1
power_at_min_n <- power_one_sample_t(min_n, cohens_d, alpha, sidedness)
power_at_preceding <- power_one_sample_t(min_n - 1, cohens_d, alpha, sidedness)

cat("Sample Size Calculation Results:\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size achieving 80% power:", min_n, "participants\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n, ":", round(power_at_min_n, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", round(power_at_preceding, 4), "\n\n")

# Verification using uniroot for continuous solution
continuous_solve <- function(n) {
  power_one_sample_t(n, cohens_d, alpha, sidedness) - target_power
}

n_continuous <- uniroot(continuous_solve, interval = c(1, 200))$root

cat("Continuous (non-integer) solution: n =", round(n_continuous, 4), "\n")
cat("Rounding convention: minimum integer satisfying power >= target\n")

# Final answer
cat("\n" + "="*50 + "\n")
cat("FINAL ANSWER:\n")
cat("Minimum sample size (integer): ", min_n, " participants\n")
cat("="*50 + "\n")

# Output for structured reporting
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_min_n, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_at_preceding, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "cohens_d", value = round(cohens_d, 4), unit = "standardized_effect_size")
  ),
  design_parameters = list(
    method = "one_sample_t",
    alpha = alpha,
    sidedness = "one-sided",
    target_power = target_power,
    mean_difference = mean_diff,
    standard_deviation = sd_value,
    hypothesis = "H0: mu=0 vs H1: mu>0"
  )
), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

library(jsonlite)

mean_diff <- 0.2
sd_value <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80

# Cohen's d effect size
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd_value

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Effect size (mean difference):", mean_diff, "units\n")
cat("Standard deviation:", sd_value, "units\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("Alpha (significance level):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Test type: One-sided one-sample t-test\n\n")

# Function to calculate power for one-sample t-test
power_one_sample_t <- function(n, d, alpha) {
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n)
  
  # Degrees of freedom
  df <- n - 1
  
  # One-sided test: upper-tail critical value
  t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
  
  # Power = P(t > t_crit | H1 is true)
  power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n that achieves target power
# Start with n=2 (df >= 1 required)
n_range <- 2:300

powers <- sapply(n_range, function(n) {
  tryCatch(power_one_sample_t(n, cohens_d, alpha), error = function(e) NA)
})

# Find minimum n with power >= target_power
valid_indices <- which(powers >= target_power)
min_n <- n_range[min(valid_indices)]

# Get power at the minimum n and at n-1
power_at_min_n <- power_one_sample_t(min_n, cohens_d, alpha)
power_at_preceding <- power_one_sample_t(min_n - 1, cohens_d, alpha)

cat("Sample Size Calculation Results:\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size achieving 80% power:", min_n, "participants\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n, ":", round(power_at_min_n, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", round(power_at_preceding, 4), "\n\n")

# Verification using uniroot for continuous solution
continuous_solve <- function(n) {
  power_one_sample_t(n, cohens_d, alpha) - target_power
}

n_continuous <- uniroot(continuous_solve, interval = c(2, 300))$root

cat("Continuous (non-integer) solution: n =", round(n_continuous, 4), "\n")
cat("Rounding convention: minimum integer satisfying power >= target\n\n")

# Final answer
cat(paste(rep("=", 60), collapse = ""), "\n")
cat("FINAL ANSWER:\n")
cat("Minimum sample size (integer):", min_n, "participants\n")
cat(paste(rep("=", 60), collapse = ""), "\n")

# Output for structured reporting
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(toJSON(list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_min_n, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_at_preceding, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "cohens_d", value = round(cohens_d, 4), unit = "standardized_effect_size"),
    list(metric = "continuous_solution", value = round(n_continuous, 4), unit = "participants_real")
  ),
  design_parameters = list(
    method = "one_sample_t",
    alpha = alpha,
    sidedness = "one-sided",
    target_power = target_power,
    mean_difference = mean_diff,
    standard_deviation = sd_value,
    hypothesis = "H0: mu=0 vs H1: mu>0"
  )
), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))

# Evidence e1; success=false

# One-sample t-test power analysis
# H0: mu = 0 vs H1: mu > 0 (one-sided)
# Effect size (Cohen's d) = mean_diff / sd

library(stats)

mean_diff <- 0.2
sd_value <- 0.5
alpha <- 0.05
target_power <- 0.80
sidedness <- 1  # one-sided

# Cohen's d effect size
cohens_d <- mean_diff / sd_value

cat("Study Design Parameters:\n")
cat("Effect size (mean difference):", mean_diff, "units\n")
cat("Standard deviation:", sd_value, "units\n")
cat("Cohen's d:", cohens_d, "\n")
cat("Alpha (significance level):", alpha, "\n")
cat("Target power:", target_power, "\n")
cat("Test type: One-sided one-sample t-test\n\n")

# Function to calculate power for one-sample t-test
# Given: effect size d, sample size n, alpha, sidedness
power_one_sample_t <- function(n, d, alpha, sidedness) {
  # Non-centrality parameter
  ncp <- d * sqrt(n)
  
  # Degrees of freedom
  df <- n - 1
  
  # For one-sided test
  if (sidedness == 1) {
    # Upper-tail critical value
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha, df)
    # Power = P(t > t_crit | H1)
    power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)
  } else {
    # Two-sided test
    t_crit <- qt(1 - alpha/2, df)
    power <- 1 - pt(t_crit, df, ncp = ncp) + pt(-t_crit, df, ncp = ncp)
  }
  
  return(power)
}

# Search for minimum n that achieves target power
# Start with a reasonable estimate and search upward
n_range <- 1:200

powers <- sapply(n_range, function(n) power_one_sample_t(n, cohens_d, alpha, sidedness))

# Find minimum n with power >= target_power
min_n <- min(n_range[powers >= target_power])

# Get power at the minimum n and at n-1
power_at_min_n <- power_one_sample_t(min_n, cohens_d, alpha, sidedness)
power_at_preceding <- power_one_sample_t(min_n - 1, cohens_d, alpha, sidedness)

cat("Sample Size Calculation Results:\n")
cat("Minimum integer sample size achieving 80% power:", min_n, "participants\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n, ":", round(power_at_min_n, 4), "\n")
cat("Power at n =", min_n - 1, ":", round(power_at_preceding, 4), "\n\n")

# Verification using uniroot for continuous solution
continuous_solve <- function(n) {
  power_one_sample_t(n, cohens_d, alpha, sidedness) - target_power
}

n_continuous <- uniroot(continuous_solve, interval = c(1, 200))$root

cat("Continuous (non-integer) solution: n =", round(n_continuous, 4), "\n")
cat("Rounding convention: minimum integer satisfying power >= target\n")

# Final answer
cat("\n" + "="*50 + "\n")
cat("FINAL ANSWER:\n")
cat("Minimum sample size (integer): ", min_n, " participants\n")
cat("="*50 + "\n")

# Output for structured reporting
cat("\nPOWER_AGENT_RESULT=")
cat(jsonlite::toJSON(list(
  results = list(
    list(metric = "sample_size", value = min_n, unit = "participants_total"),
    list(metric = "achieved_power", value = round(power_at_min_n, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "power_preceding_design", value = round(power_at_preceding, 4), unit = "proportion"),
    list(metric = "cohens_d", value = round(cohens_d, 4), unit = "standardized_effect_size")
  ),
  design_parameters = list(
    method = "one_sample_t",
    alpha = alpha,
    sidedness = "one-sided",
    target_power = target_power,
    mean_difference = mean_diff,
    standard_deviation = sd_value,
    hypothesis = "H0: mu=0 vs H1: mu>0"
  )
), auto_unbox = TRUE, digits = 15))
